sources.title: workerd — the Workers runtime, 8,643 stars, C++
Cloudflare outage on November 18, 2025 post mortem
Cloudflare to cut about 20% of its workforce

claims.text: The public GitHub organisation holds 575 repositories and six of the ten most recently touched — including the Workers runtime (workerd, C++, 8.6k stars) and workers-sdk — had commits within the last two days, so the open-source presence is live work rather than a shop window.

The company publishes detailed post-mortems on its own outages within a day, and its engineers answer questions in the resulting public threads — useful evidence about how incidents are handled internally.

The May 2026 restructuring is framed by the company itself as a move to an 'AI-first operating model', and the public discussion of it is dominated by whether that framing describes a change in how work is done or a cost cut wearing a strategy label. Worth asking directly in interviews.

gaps.reason: fewer than three independent, dated, first-hand employee accounts were found, so wlb_sentiment is left unset rather than estimated from thread tone
gaps.suggested_fallback: ask the recruiter for two current engineers on the team to speak to, and search for recent conference talks by the hiring team

eng_output_signal.note: 575 public repos, six pushed within 48 hours, including the production Workers runtime

stack_currency.note: Rust/C++/TypeScript edge runtime work; the posting's stack matches what the public repos actually run
